top_story: Houthi gains on Yemen’s Red Sea coast accelerated from the push on Mocha on 10 September to the confirmed seizure of the port and a nearby island by 11 September, placing a movement aligned with Iran closer to effective leverage over the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint and Saudi export routes. The immediate military shift expands pressure on commercial shipping and energy flows, while deepening insecurity for coastal communities already living through war, disrupted trade, and fragile access to basic goods. In Israel, renewed scrutiny of Benjamin Netanyahu over an unshared pre-7 October warning has sharpened domestic questions about political accountability and crisis leadership rather than altering the operational picture. The wider regional effect is a sharper contrast between active escalation in the Red Sea arena and intensifying legitimacy strains inside allied states confronting the consequences of security failures.
